intervals.quote: Kamioka Observatory is located in Gifu prefecture, Japan. The observatory was established in 1995

notes: The observatory also hosts KAGRA, CANDLES, NEWAGE and XENONnT R&D according to the ICRR facility page; only the Super-Kamiokande and Hyper-Kamiokande sites are recorded here.

depth.note: Rock overburden above Super-Kamiokande in the Mozumi mine.
depth.quote: 50,000-ton water Cherenkov detector located 1000m underground (2700m.w.e) in the Kamioka Mine

overburden.quote: with 1000 m of rock, or 2700 meters-water-equivalent (m.w.e.) mean overburden

summary.plain: An underground laboratory inside a mine in the Japanese Alps, a kilometre beneath a mountain. The rock above screens out most cosmic rays, so very rare signals from neutrinos can be seen.
summary.technical: Underground laboratory of the Institute for Cosmic Ray Research, University of Tokyo, in the Kamioka mine at Hida, Gifu. About 1000 m of rock (2700 m.w.e.) above Super-Kamiokande in the Mozumi mine; the Hyper-Kamiokande cavern is being built about 8 km south in the Tochibora mine.
